newsitem.title: USA: CBS wins weekly prime time TV ratings. [CORRECTED 15:39 GMT]
newsitem.headline: CBS wins weekly prime time TV ratings. [CORRECTED 15:39 GMT]

text.p: (Corrects company name throughout to Nielsen Media Research from ACNielsen Corp).

Despite NBC's hold on the top two television shows with Seinfeld and Friends, CBS won the primetime viewership ratings for the week of March 3 through March 9, Nielsen Media Research said on Wednesday.
CBS, a unit of Westinghouse Electric Corp, garnered a 9.7 rating, or 16 percent share, of all households watching television for the week, Nielsen Media said.

CBS was helped by strong performances from its Sunday night lineup of 60 Minutes, Touched by an Angel and the CBS Sunday Night Movie and Monday night shows such as Cybill, Cosby and Ink, Nielsen Media said.
Each show in CBS's Sunday lineup ranked in the top 10, Nielsen Media said.
General Electric Co's NBC finished in second place for the week with a 9.4 rating, or 16 percent share of all households watching television, Nielsen Media said.
Walt Disney Co's ABC attracted 14 percent of viewers with a rating of 8.0 percent. Home Improvement, the network's top ranked show for the week, finished in eighth place, Nielsen Media said.
News Corp's Fox nearly matched ABC's ratings by grabbing 7.7 ratings points, or 13 percent of the viewing audience.

Nielsen Media said Time Warner Inc's WB and Viacom Inc's UPN posted 2.7 points and 3.0 points, respectively. WB held four percent of the audience and UPN had five percent of the prime time audience, Nielsen Media said.
